profile.summary: FLARE (Fine-grained Learning for Alignment of spectra-molecule REpresentations) annotates metabolites from tandem mass spectra by retrieval. It embeds an MS/MS spectrum, written as chemical formulas for each peak, and candidate molecular graphs in a shared space, then ranks the candidates by similarity. The similarity is built from peak-to-atom and atom-to-peak matches, so the matches can be inspected.

summary_quotes.text: FLARE learns a joint embedding space for **MS/MS spectra** (represented as **per-peak chemical formulas** from a subformula assigner) and **molecular graphs**.
**Retrieval**: rank a list of candidate SMILES for each query spectrum (MassSpecGym-style evaluation).
FLARE computes similarity via maxima over peak-to-atom and atom-to-peak interactions, capturing chemically meaningful local correspondences and enabling interpretable spectra–molecule matching.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Peaks are first given chemical formulas by a MIST-style subformula assigner. Each formula peak is projected by a shallow MLP and contextualised by a transformer encoder, giving one embedding per peak. The molecule is a graph whose nodes carry atom features, encoded by a graph convolutional network into node embeddings. Training uses a fine-grained contrastive loss (filipContrastive): the similarity of a spectrum and a molecule averages the maximum peak-to-node and node-to-peak cosine similarities, with a temperature-scaled loss. At test time candidates are ranked by this similarity.

The spectra-molecule similarity is obtained by averaging the maximum node-to-peak similarities (not shown) and peak-to-node similarities.
The default publication model uses **fine-grained contrastive learning** (`filipContrastive`): similarity between spectrum tokens and graph nodes, with a temperature-scaled loss.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Code and the released checkpoint (pretrained_models/flare.ckpt) are distributed in the Hugging Face Space HassounLab/FLARE, which the paper names as the code location; no separate GitHub repository is named. Paper recipes are in run_scripts: the main FLARE model with candidates by mass or by formula, a global pooling baseline, and an evaluation with msbuddy-predicted formulas. The evaluation scripts use the released checkpoint by default. The Space was last modified on 2026-10-22. A result should name the Space revision, the candidate setting (mass or formula) and the formula source (ground-truth subformulae or msbuddy predictions).

sections.title: Use in benchmarks
sections.body: The MSAlign benchmark paper (an existing source on this record) ran FLARE as a retrieval baseline and describes it as a follow-up to MVP with a stronger spectrum encoder that uses subformula peak annotation and a richer, more interpretable similarity. MSAlign groups baselines by whether they need the target's molecular formula; the record description says FLARE does.

quotes.text: FLARE [13] is a direct follow-up work that considers a stronger spectra encoder leveraging peak annotation with subformulas and a more interpretable, richer similarity.
We note that some baselines require the molecular formula of the target to be provided.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Contrastive retrieval model that embeds MS/MS spectra and molecular graphs in a shared space.

quotes.text: a contrastive learning framework that leverages bidirectional peak-node alignment under learned weak supervision.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Spectrum encoder: MLP plus transformer over formula-annotated peaks (Transformer_Formula). Molecule encoder: GCN (DGL and dgllife) giving node embeddings. Loss: fine-grained contrastive (filipContrastive).

run_guide.summary: Clone the FLARE Space, install the Python requirements and start the Streamlit app, which loads the released checkpoint and plots peak-to-node correspondence for a spectrum and molecule pair.
prerequisites: A CUDA-matched PyTorch and DGL build may be needed; the README gives a DGL wheel example for CUDA 11.8.
Retrieval evaluation additionally needs the MassSpecGym files placed under data/.
